entities.summary: Liborius of Le Mans was the second Bishop of Le Mans, a diocese he played a significant role in shaping during the 4th century. He is the patron saint of the cathedral and archdiocese of Paderborn in Germany, a legacy that endures to this day. The exact date of his birth remains unknown, but his death in 397 CE is well-documented. Liborius's tenure as bishop was marked by his efforts to promote Christianity and establish the diocese as a center of learning and culture. He was succeeded by several notable bishops, including his own nephew, who continued his legacy. Liborius's legacy extends beyond his immediate successors, as he played a key role in the development of the Catholic Church in Western Europe. The cathedral of Paderborn, which he is the patron saint of, remains one of the most important architectural achievements of the Middle Ages, and its influence can still be seen in the region's architecture and culture today.
